title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page holds two 'cube' diagrams of inclusions labelled with indices. They sit in the elliptic-modular part of the Teichmüller tower: the modular stack M_{1,1}, its Legendre/level-2 cover, and their fundamental groups.

Reading of the symbols (tentative, inferred from the indices):
- 𝔖 = the modular group SL2(Z) (or its completion), i.e. π1 of M_{1,1}.
- Π = 𝔖^! = the congruence subgroup Γ(2). Up to ±1 it is the free group on two generators, π1 of P^1−{0,1,∞}, which is the λ-line. It has index 6 in 𝔖, matching [SL2(Z):Γ(2)] = 6, i.e. S3.
- Π_0 = an index-2 subgroup of Π, presumably Π/±1 or Π ∩ (kernel of a character). Then Π_0 ⊂ Π ⊂ 𝔖 has indices 2 and 6.
- Underlined Π_0 ⊂ Π = 𝔖^{+!} ⊂ 𝔖^+ are the corresponding groups in an extended version: the extended modular group GL2(Z), or the profinite/arithmetic versions, the underline possibly meaning completion.
- μ = μ_2 = {±1}, the generic automorphism group of an elliptic curve. M^! ≃ M^!_0 × μ records that the level-2 stack is a trivial μ_2-gerbe over its rigidified version.
- M, M', M^!, M^!_0 are the corresponding groups or stacks at the arithmetic or geometric level: extensions of a Galois group by 𝔖, Π, Π_0.
- M(0) is presumably the fibre or stabilizer attached to a base point 0.

Diagram III (M(0)) covers the point with extra automorphism of order 4, τ = i:
- L_0^𝔖 ⊃ L_0^Π ⊃ L_0^{Π_0} with indices 2, 2. This fits the inertia/stabilizer of i: μ_4 in SL2(Z), ±1 in Γ(2), trivial in Π_0.
- D_0^𝔖 ⊃ D_0^Π ⊃ D_0^{Π_0} are the corresponding decomposition groups: normalizer-type subgroups mapping onto the Galois group.
- μ_τ and D_τ are the local inertia and decomposition objects at τ.
- The third direction of the cube shows how everything restricts along the tower M(0) → M(0)×μ → M^! → M.
- 'M^𝔖[0] on M[0]' and 'M^Π[0] (on M^![0])' denote fibres or restrictions of the coverings over the substack of the point 0.
- The dashed arrows from M(0), μ_τ, {1} to the Π_0-level objects record the trivialisations at the deepest level.

Diagram IV (Z_ρ, N_ρ) covers the point ρ = e^{2πi/3}:
- The bottom row 1 ⊂ μ ⊂ L_ρ has indices 2, 3. So L_ρ ≅ Z/6 is the stabilizer of ρ in SL2(Z).
- Z_ρ and N_ρ are the centralizer and normalizer of L_ρ in the arithmetic group M, with Z_ρ ⊂ N_ρ.
- Z^!_ρ, Z^!_{0ρ}, N^!_ρ, N^!_{0ρ} are their intersections with the level-2 subgroups. The indices are Z^!_{0ρ} ⊂ Z^!_ρ (2) ⊂ Z_ρ (3) and Z^!_ρ ⊂ N_ρ (6).
- Product decompositions such as N^!_{0ρ} = μ_{τ'}·Z^!_{0ρ} are written explicitly.
- D_ρ and D_{τ'} are decomposition groups. M'^!_0 ⊂ M'^! ⊂ M' (indices 2, 6) is the parallel 'primed' tower. The bottom face again maps to Π_0 ⊂ Π ⊂ 𝔖^+.

Purpose: this is bookkeeping for the local structure of the modular tower at its orbifold points. It identifies inertia, decomposition, centralizer and normalizer subgroups at the points with automorphism groups μ_4 and μ_6, and how they behave under passage to the level-2 (S3) cover and its index-2 refinement. This is exactly the data that produces the order-2 and order-3 relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group and the Galois action at 'points with exceptional automorphisms' (cf. Esquisse §2–3).
errors: No clear mathematical error can be verified; the notation is private and the identification of symbols is conjectural.
In diagram IV one arrow index reads 'σ' or '6' (M'^! → M'); it should be 6 by consistency with the other rows.
Several arrows are struck out or rewritten: the label N^!_{0ρ}, and the crossed-out 'μ_{τ'}·Z^!_0' near N^!_ρ. The page is a working draft, not a final statement.

ideas.what: Lattice of inertia/decomposition groups at the elliptic points i and ρ of M_{1,1}, followed through the S3 Legendre cover and an index-2 refinement
ideas.modern_name: decomposition groups / Galois action at orbifold points (tangential and 'exceptional' base points) of M_{1,1}; local structure of the modular orbifold
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§2–3, which discusses points with extra automorphisms and the order-2 and order-3 relations from M_{1,1} and M_{0,4}

ideas.what: Centralizer Z_ρ and normalizer N_ρ of the order-6 stabilizer at ρ inside the arithmetic fundamental group, with their level-2 intersections and indices
ideas.modern_name: centralizers/normalizers of torsion in profinite (arithmetic) modular groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura (Galois rigidity, normalizers of inertia), Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps

ideas.what: M^! ≃ M^!_0 × μ: the level-2 stack splits as a trivial μ_2-gerbe over its rigidification
ideas.modern_name: rigidification of the generic ±1 automorphism (Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli rigidification)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; ACV 2003 for the general notion

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a systematic index-labelled cube of subgroups (inertia, decomposition, centralizer, normalizer) at both elliptic points of M_{1,1}, across the full tower M ⊃ M^! ⊃ M^!_0 and its extended (𝔖^+) version. The later literature treats these points case by case for the GT relations. A uniform functorial 'cube' presentation of this kind is not standard, though its content is likely known piecemeal.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest. It shows Grothendieck computing the local Galois/automorphism data at orbifold points that underlie the GT relations, rather than just stating them. It is probably not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful bookkeeping diagrams for the local group theory of the modular orbifold at its points with extra automorphisms. The content matches themes in the Esquisse and in later work by Ihara, Nakamura and Lochak–Schneps. There is no apparently new result, only working detail.
transcription_corrections: Diagram III bottom row: the transcription's L_0^{Π_0}, L_0^Π, L_0^𝔖 are drawn as L_0 with superscripts Π_0, Π, 𝔖 (the 𝔖 written as a script-S symbol). The same applies to D_0.
Diagram IV: the left label reads 'μ_{τ'}·Z^!_{0ρ} = N^!_{0ρ}' with a struck-out marker; above N^!_ρ is a crossed-out 'μ_{τ'}·Z^!_0 ...' annotation.
The arrow M'^! → M' is labelled 6 (it looks like 'σ').
In diagram IV the bottom row is 1 ↪^2 μ ↪^3 L_ρ, with L_ρ mapping down to 𝔖^+ underlined.
